title: नेपालमा छुवाछूत प्रथाको ऐतिहासिक विकास Nepalma Chuwachhut Prathako Aaitihasik Bikas
nepali: भारतीय हिन्दू समाजमा ऋग्वेदकालतिर स्थापना गरिएको वर्णव्यवस्थाका आधारमाजातिव्यवस्था विकसित भएको थियो । त्यही जातिव्यवस्थाका आधारमा विकसित भएकोछुवाछूत प्रथा अहिलेसम्म पनि नेपाली समाजमा विद्यमान रहँदै आएको छ । वर्णव्यवस्था रत्यसभित्रको छुवाछूत प्रथा नेपालमा लिच्छविकालतिर भित्रिएर मल्ल, शाह, राणा रपञ्चायतकाल हुँदै अगाडि बढ्दै आएको थियो । नेपाली समाजमा अहिले पनि यो प्रथासघन रूपमा कायमै छ । यसका विषयमा लिखित रूपमा जानकारी दिने पर्याप्त स्रोत रसामग्रीहरूको पनि अभाव रहँदै आएको छ । केही मात्रामा प्राप्त स्वदेशी र विदेशीलेखकहरूका पुस्तक तथा लेख–रचनाहरूको अध्ययन गरी वर्णनात्मक र विश्लेषणात्मकआधारमा यो लेख तयार पारिएको छ । नेपालमा विद्यमान छुवाछूत प्रथाको अन्त्यका लागिचालिएका कदममा प्रशस्त धन र समयको खर्च हुँदै आएको पाइन्छ । यस्तो हुँदा पनिअपेक्षित प्रतिफल भने प्राप्त हुनसकेको छैन । यस्तो अवस्थामा नेपाली समाजलाईविभिन्न विधिबाट सुसूचित तुल्याएर छुवाछूत जस्तो सामाजिक कलङ्कको रूपमा रहेकोयस प्रथाको अन्त्यका लागि विशेष अभियान सञ्चालन गर्नु पर्ने आवश्यकता रहेकोदेखिन्छ । यस प्रथाको अन्त्यका लागि एउटा सशक्त सामाजिक क्रान्तिको आवश्यकताखड्किदै आएको छ । यस लेखले पनि नेपालमा छुवाछूत प्रथा कहिले कसरी भित्रियो रविकसित हुँदै आएको छ भन्ने कुराको ऐतिहासिक सन्दर्भलाई खोजमूलक ढङ्गलेप्रस्ट्याउने प्रयत्न गरेको छ ।
american_english: In Indian Hindu society, the caste system had developed on the basis of the varna system, which was established around the Rigvedic period. The practice of untouchability that developed on the basis of that same caste system has remained present in Nepali society right up to the present. The varna system and the practice of untouchability within it entered Nepal around the Licchavi period and advanced forward through the Malla, Shah, Rana and Panchayat periods. Even now this practice remains firmly in place in Nepali society in an intensive form. There has also been a continuing lack of sufficient sources and materials that provide written information on this subject. By studying the books and writings of native and foreign authors available only in limited quantity, this article has been prepared on a descriptive and analytical basis. It is found that considerable money and time have been spent on the steps taken to end the practice of untouchability existing in Nepal. Yet even so, the expected results have not been obtained. In such a situation, there appears to be a need to raise awareness among Nepali society through various methods and to run a special campaign to end this practice, which persists as a social stigma like untouchability. The need for a strong social revolution to end this practice is emerging. This article has also attempted to set forth, in an exploratory manner, the historical background of when and how the practice of untouchability entered Nepal and developed.
british_english: In Indian Hindu society, the caste system had evolved on the basis of the varna system, which was established around the time of the Rigveda. The custom of untouchability, which developed on the basis of that same caste system, has continued to exist in Nepali society right down to the present day. The varna system, together with the custom of untouchability within it, entered Nepal around the Licchavi period and went forward through the Malla, Shah, Rana and Panchayat eras. Even today this custom remains firmly entrenched in Nepali society in a pervasive form. There has likewise been a persistent shortage of adequate sources and material giving written information on the subject. By examining the books and writings of native and foreign authors, which are available only in limited quantity, this article has been produced on a descriptive and analytical footing. It is evident that substantial sums of money and time have been expended on the measures taken to bring an end to the custom of untouchability prevailing in Nepal. Nevertheless, the anticipated results have not been achieved. In these circumstances it would appear necessary to inform Nepali society thoroughly through a variety of means and to mount a special campaign to end this custom, which continues as a social stigma in the manner of untouchability. The need for a powerful social revolution to end this custom is coming to the fore. This article has likewise endeavoured to set out, in an investigative manner, the historical context of when and how the custom of untouchability entered Nepal and developed.
australian_english: In Indian Hindu society, the caste system developed on the basis of the varna system, which was set up around the time of the Rigveda. The practice of untouchability that grew out of that same caste system has stayed around in Nepali society right up to today. The varna system and the practice of untouchability inside it came into Nepal around the Licchavi period and moved forward through the Malla, Shah, Rana and Panchayat periods. Even now the practice remains firmly in place in Nepali society in a concentrated form. There has also been a lasting shortage of enough sources and materials that give written information about this subject. By looking at the books and essays of local and foreign writers that are only available in small numbers, this article has been put together on a descriptive and analytical basis. It turns out that plenty of money and time have gone into the steps being taken to end the practice of untouchability that exists in Nepal. Yet the results that were expected have not come through. In a situation like this, it looks like there is a need to get Nepali society properly informed through different methods and to run a special campaign to end this practice, which sticks around as a social stigma like untouchability. The need for a strong social revolution to end this practice is starting to emerge. This article has also tried to lay out, in an exploratory way, the historical background of when and how the practice of untouchability came into Nepal and developed.
